preamble: A prothetic [e] is added before a word-initial cluster of s plus consonant, giving the cluster a syllable to begin with. Early Western Romance did this to Latin s impurum (status > Spanish estado, schola > Old French escole), and Spanish still does it to loanwords such as estrés and esnob. Basque, which has no initial s plus consonant, adds e- to Latin and modern loans (espiritu, eslogan).

examples.note: Prothetic e- before s + stop, inherited from early Romance; also schola > escuela.
The same constraint applies to modern loanwords; also escáner from English scanner.
Prothetic e- was added before s + consonant; the s was later lost before the consonant.
Modern French spécial was later re-formed on the Latin model.
Basque has no word-initial s + consonant, so an e- (more rarely i-) is added.
Same prothesis in a modern loanword.
